discrepancies.topic: Stack direction and R6 behavior
discrepancies.sources: The community wiki (SRC-intv-wiki) is read as saying R6 auto-increments on indirect reads and auto-decrements on indirect writes, which is the reverse of the manual. A community transcription of the manual (SRC-community-emu-docs) agrees with the manual: post-increment on output (push), pre-decrement on input (pull), and its interrupts document has the stack growing upward. That transcription was damaged by character recognition, so the manual page images were read directly.
discrepancies.default_policy: resolved: R6 is post-incremented after an indirect output (push) and pre-decremented before an indirect input (pull); the stack grows toward higher addresses; the interrupt entry stores the PC at the address held in R6 and then increments R6.

discrepancies.topic: GRAM extent and STIC decode range
discrepancies.sources: GRAM is at $3800-$39FF mirrored at $3A00-$3FFF in some research files and $3800-$3AFF with a shadow to $3FFF in others. STIC registers are $0000-$007F in one file and respond at $00-$3F with decoding of $0000-$007F in others. The 1980 catalog places the GROM at $3000-$37FF after an SR1 pulse and addresses external memory at $3800-$3FFF in that view (SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-16, pdf 197), which supports a GRAM decode across the whole 2K window but gives no RAM size. Community documents disagree on whether $3A00-$3FFF accepts writes (SRC-intv-wiki, Memory Map oldid 14847, says read/write; another research file says not writable).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: GRAM at $3800-$39FF mirrored to $3FFF and STIC decode over $0000-$007F, both tagged and minor.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 read-back of GRAM writes at $3800-$3FFF and of STIC register reads at $0000-$007F on owner hardware; the Phase 3 memory-map tests only check consistency with the chosen default
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by the 64-row register literal and the alias set of the profile (stic.regmap, stic.access_effects) and the GRAM mirror of the memory map; exercised by stic.alias.write-4000, stic.alias.write-8000, stic.alias.write-C000, stic.alias.read-0040, memmap.mirror.gram-3a00, memmap.anchor.stic-regs-lo, memmap.anchor.stic-regs-hi, memmap.anchor.gram-hi and the fault STIC_ALIAS_NOT_HOOKED.
discrepancies.note: Seeded from the research source-conflict table. Plan 06-01 (D-04, A-01): the STIC decode range and alias set are modelled by the register literal (64 rows) and C84; the card path never forms an address above $39FF. Tests: stic.alias.*.

discrepancies.topic: Fixture assembler
discrepancies.sources: One research file recommends a pinned dev-time-only assembler from the GPL community fork (SRC-community-emu-docs) with a second assembler cross-check and a deferred project assembler. Another recommends a project-authored mini-assembler. Two more say either.

discrepancies.topic: Reference PCM location
discrepancies.sources: One research file puts integer-only reference PCM decimation inside the core's observation layer, another derives host PCM outside the core, and a third says host resampling must stay out of the evidence path. All agree raw chip-rate output must be distinct from host PCM. Decided as D7 (D-21, owner authorization 2026-11-09): no PCM, resampling, DAC-table use or WAV code in the core or any installed artifact; a pure integer reference converter outside the core is operator-side only.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: raw chip-rate output (post-mixer effective level per channel) is distinct from host PCM; the core derives no PCM; the DAC table psg.dac.levels stays unknown-default-chosen (C12) and only hosts and the reference converter read it.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 5 raw-audio tests and the converter repeatability tests (plans 05-06 and 05-10)
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): partial, D7 as decided. The core derives no PCM: control core-symbols-pcm-defined, psg.dac.not-in-core and psg.profile.dac-levels-not-read-by-core (field psg.dac.levels, inference, C12). The reference converter lives in tools/pcm, outside the core and every installed artifact, and is exercised by runner.refpcm.* (13 cases), the judge self-controls runner.judge.refpcm-floor-rounding, runner.judge.refpcm-dc-state-carry and runner.judge.refpcm-rate-drift, runner-process.refpcm.wav-written and runner-process.refpcm.diag-ctrl-psg-pass (the .refpcm golden, repeatability only). Resolved-primary would need a primary source; none applies.
discrepancies.note: Seeded from the research source-conflict table. Phase 5 (D-21): partial, not resolved-primary: the location is decided on architecture grounds, not by a primary page.

discrepancies.topic: CI shape
discrepancies.sources: One research file recommends Linux gcc and clang with sanitizers, fuzz smoke if cheap, one macOS job and scheduled memory and thread sanitizer jobs. Another defers fuzzing and matrix growth until a failure class justifies them, and a third calls more than three required jobs a performance trap.

discrepancies.resolver: test: ci-parity bans and ci-log
discrepancies.note: Seeded from the research source-conflict table. D12 decided as Phase 4 D-41..D-45 (one ubuntu-24.04 job, no matrix, no caches or artifacts, job summary, run record); recorded by plan 04-25. It stays open because the shape is a budgeted default with reversal triggers, not a settled fact.

discrepancies.sources: One research file makes a mini-EXEC first-class from the first slice. Another labels it not an EXEC. A third warns against writing an EXEC replacement casually because its contract must be tested and its presence changes timing. A fourth calls the EXEC-less reset story an owner or profile question.

discrepancies.sources: One research file has reset at $1000 and the interrupt service entry at $1004. Another adds dispatch at $1004 through a vector at $0100 and $0101 in double-byte form and a NOP at $1009 so a bus request can be serviced (SRC-community-emu-docs). A third says reset sets R7 to $1000 at low confidence. The sources are consistent on $1000 and $1004; the dispatch details come from one source.

discrepancies.sources: The GPL community fork is GPL-2.0 with a readme saying GPL v2 or later, and is based on a 2020-08-22 snapshot. The official page lists 20200712 as the current stable release and the upstream site was unreachable during research. A header in one example library is CC0 while its examples readme is GPL (SRC-community-emu-docs).

discrepancies.topic: Branch cycle count printed 7/9 with no taken or not-taken label
discrepancies.sources: The branch table prints 7/9 for the unconditional branch, for each condition row that carries a count, and for the external-condition branch, and prints a single 7 for the two-word NOPP form, with no label saying which figure applies when the branch is taken (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). The one branch timing figure found shows only the fetch of the displacement and does not settle it.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: Phase 2 reads the first printed figure (7) as not taken and the second (9) as taken for rows that print 7/9, as a named policy; the manual does not state this.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 2 branch cycle vectors; a bus trace of taken and not-taken branches (D10) would settle it
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 54 (7/9 rows, NOPP prints 7); pdf 32 (displacement fetch only); S3.2.2, pdf 47. See the Branch timing section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21). Open item for Phase 2: the 7/9 column.

discrepancies.topic: Interrupt-entry cycle count is not tabulated
discrepancies.sources: The manual gives the interrupt sequence as INTAK, NACT, DW, DWS, NACT, IAB, three NACT and then the first fetch address output, but the instruction summary tables carry no entry cycle count (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: Phase 2 uses nine CPU cycles from counting the time-slot groups on the timing diagram, labelled inference and not a printed figure.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 2 interrupt-entry vectors; a bus trace of an interrupt acceptance (D10) would settle it
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 35 (timing diagram); pdf 53 to pdf 58 (no entry count tabulated); SC.6, pdf 24 and pdf 25. See the Interrupt sequence section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21).

discrepancies.topic: The manual describes the CP-1600, not the CP-1610
discrepancies.sources: The pages read describe the CP-1600 throughout and the electrical specifications section is headed Tentative (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). The 1980 catalog lists the CP1610 used in the console (SRC-gi-1980-catalog).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the manual's encodings, cycle counts and sequences are applied to the CP1610 as the nearest primary source, with the Tentative marking recorded.
discrepancies.resolver: pending: a CP1610 datasheet page that states the same encodings, cycle counts and sequences
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 12; pdf 14; S2.4, pdf 38 (heading Tentative). See the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21).

discrepancies.topic: Reset PC is supplied by a device over the bus through IAB, not by a fixed vector
discrepancies.sources: The manual says the CPU inputs the starting address from the bus when MSYNC* is released, that the address may be user-defined or the default from the non-driven bus state, and that registers and status bits are undefined after initialization (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). The profile's $1000 for R7 comes from community sources (SRC-community-emu-docs) and is not a manual fact.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: R7 is $1000 at reset as a profile default (field reset.r7), with other registers and flags zero, until the bus rule and the system image are decided.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 reset read-back on owner hardware (D5 decided as D-24: user-supplied system images only, project boot stub in Phase 4)
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 SC.1, pdf 21; Fig. 2-6, pdf 22; pdf 27. See the Reset, MSYNC and IAB section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21). Profile fields reset.r7, reset.registers_other and reset.flags are the non-manual defaults.

discrepancies.topic: Shift mode-bit names do not match the shift mnemonic names for left shifts
discrepancies.sources: The figure says A = 0 is logical or rotate, yet the SLL row is the pattern with B L A = 0 0 1, which is A = 1, while the SWAP row has A = 0 (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the shift table is taken as the operative statement and the figure names are not used to derive encodings.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 2 shift vectors read together with the figure and the table
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 S3.3.2, pdf 50; pdf 53. See the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21).

discrepancies.topic: SDBD indirect cycle counts may or may not include the SDBD row
discrepancies.sources: The manual prints a 4-cycle SDBD row followed by a 10-cycle instruction row for the indirect forms, against a single 14 for the immediate pairs (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: Phase 2 adds the 4-cycle SDBD row to the printed instruction row and flags the total as ambiguous.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 2 SDBD cycle vectors; a worked example in the manual or a bus trace would settle it
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 57 (indirect SDBD table); pdf 58 (immediate pairs).
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21). Open item for Phase 2. Plan 02-17: the isolated second readers of sdbd.json and interrupt.json read the immediate-pair 14 (pdf 58) as the target alone, so their pairs total 18; the adjudication kept the default (pdf 58 prints the 14 against a row that begins with the SDBD word, matching the 4 + 10 split of pdf 57) and the item stays open (data/cp1610/vector-review.json).

discrepancies.topic: Stop behavior wording differs between pages
discrepancies.sources: One page says a stop request takes effect only after an interruptible instruction completes, while the start/stop section says after the completion of an instruction; the HLT row of the instruction table makes no statement (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the stop takes effect at the next instruction boundary, the wider wording, until the HLT row and a bus trace say otherwise.
discrepancies.resolver: test: Phase 2 stop and halt vectors; a bus trace would settle it
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 14; S4.4, pdf 74; pdf 56. See the Start and stop section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md.
discrepancies.note: Appended from the Discrepancy candidates section of docs/cp1610/reference-notes.md (D-21).

discrepancies.topic: Access offsets inside an instruction outside the printed timing figures are inference
discrepancies.sources: The manual prints bus timing figures only for some instruction classes (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 27-37); every other in-instruction access offset is not tabulated.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: access offsets are asserted exactly only for classes with a printed timing figure; elsewhere they are tagged inference and the printed cycle totals stay authoritative (D-12).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 access-schedule vectors for classes with a printed figure; measurement: D10 bus trace on owner hardware would settle the rest
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 27-37 (timing figures); pdf 53-58 (cycle totals).
discrepancies.note: Recorded before implementation per D-13. Cycle totals are never derived from the inferred offsets.

discrepancies.topic: SDBD modes 1-3: one word versus the same byte twice
discrepancies.sources: Page 47 says the double-byte-data mode reads only one word for the multi-word modes; page 57 says the instruction will access the same byte twice, and Fig. 3.2.6 on page 49 prints one cycle count for all modes (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: SDBD modes 1-3 do two reads at the same address and the register is not incremented (POL-SDBD-01, A-03); modes 4 and 5 do two reads and two increments.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 SDBD vectors for modes 1-3 (policy kind); measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 47 (one word); pdf 57 (same byte twice); Fig. 3.2.6, pdf 49.
discrepancies.note: RESEARCH gap G7 is this entry (A-06 mapping G1 = C46, G2 = C47, G3 = C48, G4 = C49, G5 = C50, G6 = C51, G7 = C37, G8 = C58). Flip trigger: a contrary primary reading.

discrepancies.topic: Line sampling point
discrepancies.sources: The manual does not say at which tick within a unit the interrupt and bus request lines are sampled (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the machine layer samples the lines once per interruptible boundary at unit end minus one CPU cycle (POL-LINE-01); the CPU only receives the sampled values.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 interrupt boundary vectors; measurement: D10 line-edge probe; revisit in Phase 6 STIC races
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22 (interrupt entry); pdf 36 (bus request timing). Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by profile field bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles = 1 (4 ticks), applied at every unit start by the machine step seam and ivs_stic_lines in core/src/stic/stic_lines.c; the stepper is unchanged; exercised by stic.lines.sampling-lag, stic.lines.pure-of-start-tick, stic.irq.eis-late-misses and the fault STIC_LINE_LAG_IGNORED.
discrepancies.note: A machine-layer rule: the CPU never sees ticks (D-05). Plan 06-01 (D-08): POL-LINE-01 is promoted to the profile field bus.line_sample_lag_cpu_cycles = 1 (lag 4 ticks) with the same status; the INTRM and BUSRQ predicates are in docs/stic/timing-notes.md.

discrepancies.topic: Strobe stamps for TCI and PCIT
discrepancies.sources: The timing figures print the TCI pulse after the instruction end and the PCIT pulse inside the software interrupt cycle (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the TCI pulse is stamped at unit end plus 1 CPU cycle (pdf 33) and the PCIT pulse falls inside the 6-cycle SIN (pdf 34) (D-12).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 control-class vectors for TCI and SIN pulse stamps; measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 33 (TCI); pdf 34 (SIN, PCIT).
discrepancies.note: Pulse events may be stamped up to 1 cycle past the unit end (D-12).

discrepancies.topic: HLT sets a stop latch that wins at the next interruptible boundary
discrepancies.sources: One page says a stop takes effect after an interruptible instruction; the start and stop section says after an instruction; the HLT row is silent about interrupt and bus request priority (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). Community lists call HLT non-interruptible.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: HLT sets a stop latch evaluated at the next interruptible boundary with priority over BUSRQ and INTR; the stopped state is terminal until resume or reset (POL-HLT-01).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 stop and halt vectors (sequence INSTR, INSTR, HALTED); measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 14; pdf 56 (HLT row); S4.4, pdf 74.
discrepancies.note: Refines C35. Low confidence (about 50 percent); flip trigger: a bus trace showing an interrupt accepted after HLT.

discrepancies.topic: Interrupt acceptance does not clear the interrupt enable flip-flop; JE takes effect before the boundary test
discrepancies.sources: The manual says EIS, JE and JSRE enable the interrupt system and DIS, JD and JSRD disable it, and that a terminated interrupt returns control, without stating that acceptance clears the enable (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: interrupt acceptance does not clear INTFF, and JE takes effect before the boundary test (POL-INT-03); profile field cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff = 0, with vectors for both values.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 interrupt-entry vectors for both flag values; measurement: D10 repeated-interrupt probe
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22; pdf 56 (EIS, DIS, TCI); pdf 52 (JE, JD). Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by profile field cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff = 0; the consequence is stated in docs/stic/timing-notes.md (a service routine that does not start with DIS is re-entered at every open boundary while the level is held, about 250 entries per frame); exercised by stic.irq.level-held-reentry-c41-0, stic.irq.dis-first-isr-one-entry, stic.irq.c41-both-values, stic.irq.dis-blocks (in-process stand-in routines). The diagnostic ivs-diag-stic-1 has no interrupt routine at all (the boot stub has none), so the DIS-first rule is exercised by the stand-ins only and a project interrupt routine is a Phase 7 need.
discrepancies.note: Profile field cpu.interrupt_accept_clears_intff holds 0 (false) as a JSON number. Plan 06-01 (D-08): consequence stated: with a level held 3,791 cycles and the flip-flop not cleared on acceptance, a service routine that does not start with DIS is re-entered at every open boundary until the level falls (about 250 entries per frame); every Phase 6 original diagnostic routine is DIS-first, and a vector family covers both field values.

discrepancies.topic: Interrupt vector value answered on the IAB access
discrepancies.sources: The manual says the interrupt vector is obtained from the bus through the IAB access (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22); the value 0x1004 comes from community sources (SRC-community-emu-docs), like the reset value in C32.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the core holds no vector constant; the bus layer answers the IAB access, with profile field interrupt.iab_value = $1004 for the first profile (POL-IAB-01).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 IAB-provider vectors with arbitrary 16-bit values; measurement: D10 interrupt vector read-back on owner hardware
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22; pdf 27; see C32 for the reset analogue.
discrepancies.note: Tier 4 community value; the core only loads whatever the bus returns into R7.

discrepancies.topic: Residual shared-misreading risk in hand-derived vectors
discrepancies.sources: The same model family reads the manual pages, writes the expected values and writes the code, so a shared misreading can pass every vector (D-15, D-16).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: vectors are hand-derived from the page images with a blinded second reading and sensitivity controls; the residual risk is recorded rather than claimed closed.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 blinded second-reader comparison; measurement: Phase 4 original diagnostic ROMs and D10 hardware probes close it
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 page images read in plan 01-02; see data/cp1610/second-reader.json.
discrepancies.note: Not closable inside this phase. Evidence tier of every vector stays source-expectation.

discrepancies.topic: PCIT as an input is not modelled
discrepancies.sources: The manual describes a pin that, when asserted during a fetch, suppresses the program counter increment (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: PCIT as an input is not modelled; the lines record has no field for it (A-01); PCIT is reported only as an output pulse (C39).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 lines-record vectors show no input path; measurement: none planned
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 13.
discrepancies.note: Revisit if a profile needs PCIT-driven fetch control.

discrepancies.topic: HALTED state with INTR, INTRM and BUSRQ
discrepancies.sources: The manual does not state how the stopped state treats interrupt requests or bus requests (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the HALTED state ignores INTR and INTRM and still honours BUSRQ (A-10, RESEARCH A6).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 halted-state vectors; measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 14; pdf 36.
discrepancies.note: Resume or reset is the only exit from HALTED.

discrepancies.topic: CMP operand direction (RESEARCH G1)
discrepancies.sources: CMPR, CMP and CMP@ say compare with by subtraction without naming the operand order; CMPI says from the contents of register SSS (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: CMP computes register minus operand; carry is the carry-out of register plus the two's complement of the operand.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 arithmetic vectors cpu.CMP* (flags); measurement: D10 flag read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 45; pdf 53; pdf 55; pdf 57.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G1 = C46.

discrepancies.topic: S after right shifts and SWAP (RESEARCH G2)
discrepancies.sources: The shift header says right shifts set S with bit 7 of the result, and the SWAP row says S equals bit 7 of the result (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: S is bit 7 of the result after right shifts and SWAP; left shifts use the generic rule (S is bit 15).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 shift vectors cpu.SLR* and cpu.SWAP*; measurement: D10 flag read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 53.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G2 = C47.

discrepancies.topic: Link-bit positions of RLC and RRC (RESEARCH G3)
discrepancies.sources: For N=1 the manual gives RLC with C as bit 17 and OV as bit 16, and RRC with C as bit 16 and OV as bit 17, and says RLC and RRC use OV as an input (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: RLC and RRC with N=1 use the 18-bit string with the stated link positions and OV as an input; with N=0 OV is preserved.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 shift vectors with initial OV = 1; measurement: D10 flag read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 53.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G3 = C48.

discrepancies.topic: C and OV of NEGR, ADCR and RSWD (RESEARCH G4)
discrepancies.sources: Section 3.1.2 names only add, subtract and compare for carry and overflow, while the NEGR, ADCR and RSWD rows list C and OV as changed (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: NEGR, ADCR and RSWD set C and OV by analogy with section 3.1.2: NEGR is zero minus the operand by two's complement addition, ADCR is the operand plus C.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 arithmetic and control vectors cpu.NEGR*, cpu.ADCR*, cpu.RSWD*; measurement: D10 flag read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 45; pdf 53; pdf 56.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G4 = C49. Tag inference in each derivation.

discrepancies.topic: Backward branch displacement width (RESEARCH G5)
discrepancies.sources: The manual says a backward branch adds the one's complement of the displacement word to the address after the branch, without stating the width, and its printed range mixes bases (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: for a backward branch the 16-bit one's complement of the displacement word is added to PC+2; the range text is not used for derivation.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 branch vectors, backward direction; measurement: D10 branch probe
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 47; pdf 54.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G5 = C50.

discrepancies.topic: Width of operand, direct-address, jump-address and displacement words (RESEARCH G6)
discrepancies.sources: The direct address is aaaaaa AAAAAAAAAA with six high bits that depend on memory width, and the jump address uses bits 7..2 of the second word and bits 9..0 of the third (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: operand, direct-address, jump-address and displacement words keep all 16 bits on the flat test bus; only the first decle of an instruction ignores bits 15..10 (POL-ILL-01).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 policy vectors for wide words; measurement: D10 read-back of the upper bits of a non-GI cartridge ROM
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 48; pdf 52. Plan 03-04: ROM upper bits read 0 for the GI mask ROM parts (SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13, pdf 194; printed 5-21, pdf 202), so profile device rom10 reads (stored & $03FF); operand words on the flat CPU test bus keep 16 bits.
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G6 = C51.

discrepancies.topic: Bus request release latency and the grant leading into the interrupt test
discrepancies.sources: The bus timing diagram shows the grant and release but not a numeric release latency (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 36).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: BUSRQ release latency is 2 CPU cycles (inference); prev_interruptible survives a bus grant and the grant leads into the interrupt test, not into a fetch (POL-BUS-01, A-02); profile field bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles = 2.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 bus-grant vectors with BUSRQ and INTR together; measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 22; pdf 36. Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by profile field bus.release_latency_cpu_cycles = 2 (inference), part of the closed form w + 468 ticks of a bus window and of the 13 cycles per frame per added cycle of latency; exercised by stic.busrq.closed-form-resume, stic.busrq.halted-grants, stic.bounds.g-and-u-full-machine, stic.steal.accounting, stic.tile.units-equal-elapsed and the fault STIC_GRANT_RELEASE_LATENCY_DROPPED.
discrepancies.note: Confidence about 60 percent. Plan 06-01 (D-09, A-09): load-bearing from Phase 6: every added cycle of release latency adds 13 cycles per frame; the closed form w + 4 x (H + 1 + L) = w + 468 ticks. Tests: stic.steal.*, stic.tile.*.

discrepancies.topic: Bus wait rule and cap
discrepancies.sources: The manual says wait states follow the address phase and that a device must answer in under 40 microseconds (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 12, 40, 43).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: BDRDY waits apply only to accesses that begin with a BAR or ADAR address phase, which are FETCH, READ, WRITE and ADAR; INTAK, IAB and DW (the interrupt-entry write, reported as its own access kind) take none; the cap is 35 CPU cycles, from less than 40 microseconds at the D2 cycle (POL-WAIT-01, A-04, A-11); profile field bus.wait_limit_cpu_cycles = 35.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 wait vectors including no-wait-on-DW; measurement: D10 slow-device probe
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 12; pdf 40; pdf 43.
discrepancies.note: Exceeding the cap is a sticky fault (BUS_WAIT_LIMIT).

discrepancies.topic: STPST is an edge event and one latch serves HLT and STPST
discrepancies.sources: The manual describes the stop request as an event that takes effect at a boundary, not as a level (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: STPST is an edge event; one stop latch serves HLT and STPST; a second edge before the boundary cancels a pending stop (A-01).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 stop-edge vectors; measurement: D10 bus trace
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 14.
discrepancies.note: Complements C40.

discrepancies.topic: Destination equal to the pointer register
discrepancies.sources: The manual does not say what happens when the destination register of an indirect instruction is also the pointer register (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: when DDD equals the pointer register (MVI@ R4,R4 or PULR R6) the result wins over the increment; the increment happens before the operation, so ADD@ R4,R4 sees R4+1 (POL-STK-02).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 indirect-mode vectors cpu.MVI@ and cpu.PULR with DDD equal to the pointer; measurement: D10 register read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 48; pdf 55.
discrepancies.note: Applies to R4, R5 and R6. Plan 02-17: the isolated second reader of indirect.json, whose policy statement lacked the increment-order clause, used the old R4 for ADD@ R4,R4; the adjudication kept the default from the pdf 48 order (the increment is part of address formation, which precedes the operation) and completed the statement in docs/cp1610/second-reader-policies.md.

discrepancies.topic: Interruptibility of HLT, SDBD and the MVO family
discrepancies.sources: The manual marks shifts, EIS, DIS, TCI, CLRC and SETC as not interruptible and is silent on HLT, SDBD and the MVO family; SIN is shown as a software interrupt (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). Related to C19.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: HLT, SDBD and the MVO family (MVO, MVO@, MVOI, PSHR) are non-interruptible by default; SIN is interruptible (POL-INT-02).
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 per-opcode interruptibility vectors; measurement: D10 interrupt-injection probe
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 13; pdf 56.
discrepancies.note: Vector lists are literal, not generated from a table.

discrepancies.topic: External condition provider for BEXT
discrepancies.sources: The manual describes the BEXT branch as testing an external condition input without stating its idle level (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the BEXT external condition provider defaults to false, stored as profile value 0 (POL-BR-01); profile field cpu.ebci_default = 0.
discrepancies.resolver: test: phase-2 BEXT vectors with at least two E codes; measurement: D10 pin read-back
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 32; pdf 54.
discrepancies.note: Profile field cpu.ebci_default holds 0 (false) as a JSON number.

discrepancies.topic: JSR return address (RESEARCH G8)
discrepancies.sources: The reference notes call the last digit of the return address smudged on page 52; page 56 prints Return address (PC+3) legibly in the JSR, JSRE and JSRD rows (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975).
discrepancies.default_policy: resolved: JSR, JSRE and JSRD store PC+3 in R4, R5 or R6 as designated by the two BB bits (BB not 11), matching the C17 stack-shape resolution.
discrepancies.resolver: test: plan 02-12 jump vectors cpu.J.jsr-r4-return, cpu.J.jsr-r5-return, cpu.J.jsr-r6-return and fault JSR_RETURN_ADDR
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 ... pdf 56; pdf 52 (smudged).
discrepancies.note: A-06 mapping: G8 = C58. Read from the page image gi-056 in plan 02-01.

discrepancies.topic: SWAP with N = 1: register restored versus another two-byte result
discrepancies.sources: The SWAP row of the shift table says N = 1 swaps the bytes of register RR and then swaps them back to original form, so the register value is unchanged and only S and Z are set (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975). Community programming descriptions of the CP-1610 are reported to give a different N = 1 result, such as the low byte copied into the high byte; that report is background knowledge, not re-read for this entry, and no emulator source was consulted.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: SWAP with N = 1 leaves the register value unchanged (swap, then swap back), sets S from bit 7 and Z from the 16-bit result (C47), keeps C and OV, and takes 8 cycles.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 register read-back after SWAP Rn, 2 with distinct high and low bytes in an original diagnostic
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 53 (SWAP row and shift header); Fig 3.3.2, pdf 50.
discrepancies.note: Raised by the phase 2 code review (WR-05). The vector cpu.SWAP.n1 encodes the manual reading (kind source); its derivation does not yet cite this entry because shift.json is pinned by its second-read record (A-12), so the cite waits for the next re-read of that file. The core cites C59 at the SWAP handler.

discrepancies.topic: Upper bits of 8-bit RAM, PSG and STIC register reads
discrepancies.sources: The GI mask ROMs drive zero on the bits above their width (RO-3-9502 and RO-3-9504 bits 15..10, SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13 and 5-21, pdf 194 and 202; RO-3-9503 GROM bits 15..8, printed 5-16, pdf 197). No tier 1 to 3 source states what bits 15..8 of the 8-bit scratchpad and GRAM RAMs, or bits of the PSG and STIC registers, read as on a 2609. One community data point on a different board agrees with zero for 8-bit RAM. Phase 5 (plan 05-01): the PSG register map writes and reads only the low byte of the 16-bit bus word (psg.regmap, tier 4, C70); upper bits of the PSG registers and ports read 0 by default (memmap.device.psg8).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: scratchpad and GRAM upper byte read 0; stub registers read the undriven fill FFFF
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 read-back of scratchpad, GRAM, PSG and STIC register reads on owner hardware
discrepancies.evidence: SRC-gi-1980-catalog printed 5-13, pdf 194; printed 5-16, pdf 197; printed 5-21, pdf 202 (the tier 1 zero applies to the GI mask ROM and GROM parts only). Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by profile fields memmap.device.ram8, memmap.device.stub and, for the STIC registers, memmap.device.stic14 (read value $FFFF except the collision registers); exercised by stic.reg.write-only-reads-ffff, stic.reg.collision-readback, memmap.width.stic14-registers, memmap.width.undriven-reads-ffff.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 03-04 (D-23). Profile fields memmap.device.ram8 and memmap.device.stub reference this entry. Plan 06-01: STIC registers: see C81 (read-back) and C86 (widths); the register literal records every row.

discrepancies.topic: Write-only STIC and GRAM aliases coexisting with cartridge ROM
discrepancies.sources: A community memory map lists write-only STIC aliases at $4000-$403F, $8000-$803F and $C000-$C03F and write-only GRAM aliases at $7800-$7FFF, $B800-$BFFF and $F800-$FFFF, and states that cartridge ROM may still be read there (SRC-intv-wiki, Memory Map oldid 14847). One community lineage; no tier 1 to 3 source.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: reads return cartridge ROM when a segment is loaded there, else the undriven fill; writes reach the alias device (GRAM backing or the stub STIC registers) whether or not a segment is loaded
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 write and read-back through an alias address with and without a cartridge segment on owner hardware
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by the alias regions of the profile and the read view of the memory system (a loaded segment is read, the alias device is written); exercised by stic.alias.read-4021-returns-read-view-value, stic.alias.write-4000, stic.alias.write-8000, stic.alias.write-C000, memmap.cart.under-gram-alias.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 03-04 (D-23). The alias regions of the profile reference this entry. Plan 06-01: the alias read sensitivity of the mode-select addresses is C84; the alias window set is part of the register literal.

discrepancies.topic: Cartridge span of the first profile
discrepancies.sources: Community documents list cartridge-usable ranges inside $4000-$FFFF and lower ranges near $0500, $0D00 and $2000, some of them conditional on attached peripherals (SRC-intv-wiki, Memory Map oldid 14847; SRC-community-emu-docs). The same documents describe cartridge segments on 256-word boundaries; that alignment is recorded here as a tier 4 note only and is not a Phase 3 rule (A-01). No tier 1 to 3 source gives the 2609 cartridge decode.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the cartridge span is $4000-$FFFF; a segment may start at any address inside it and must not overlap another segment; lower holes are not opened
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 cartridge decode probe on owner hardware, or a tier 1 to 3 board source
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 03-04 (D-23, A-01, A-02). Profile field memmap.cart_span references this entry. Widening the span later is additive; narrowing it is a claim change.

discrepancies.topic: Disc internals and two disc positions closed together
discrepancies.sources: SRC-bsr-2609 gives the disc a 5-bit code for 16 directions. SRC-intv-wiki (Hand Controller, oldid 14808) gives key codes and combination rules but no disc contact structure. No source says whether two disc positions can be closed at once or what the port reads then.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the 16 disc positions are independent logical bits (IVS_CTRL_*); a word may set more than one, and the byte function takes the union of the lines of every closed switch (pins = 0xFF XOR OR of the line masks). Policy rows in data/expected/input-policies.ids: two adjacent disc positions, two non-adjacent positions, opposite directions and three or more controls are unknown-default-chosen results of the union rule, never evidence of what hardware reads.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 controller reader diagnostic on owner hardware: each disc position singly and adjacent pairs where mechanically possible, on each port
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field input.line_model (ground-union, inference) carries the union rule; the policy rows of data/expected/input-policies.ids are exercised by input.combo.discn-discnne and input.combo.disce-discese (adjacent), input.combo.discn-disce and input.combo.discnne-discese (other), input.combo.opposite-n-s, opposite-e-w, opposite-ne-sw, opposite-nw-se (opposite directions), input.combo.three-key1-key9-discn, input.combo.three-discn-disce-discs and input.combo.all-closed (three or more), and by input.pairs.union, commutative, monotone-clear and decodable-claims. They show the union rule, never what a controller reads. Hardware items: D10-INP-06, D10-INP-07.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-13 (D-16, D6). Nothing reads the controller words in Phase 4, so no Phase 4 result depends on it. Phase 5 (D-03): the policy classes are pinned in data/expected/input-policies.ids.

discrepancies.topic: Unplugged connector and upper-byte read
discrepancies.sources: SRC-intv-wiki (Hand Controller, oldid 14808) states that an idle controller reads all 1s in the low 8 bits (active-low). No source gives the read of a port with no controller attached, or the upper 8 bits of a CPU read of an 8-bit port.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: an unplugged connector reduces to an idle port by inference (all ones in the low byte, the same as an idle controller); the upper byte of a port read is $00 (device kind psg8 fill, D-04), a default with one weak source (illustrative wiki code), and stays open.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: read both ports with no controller attached and with an idle controller, recording the full 16-bit read
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile fields input.line_idle (tier4-community) and, for the upper byte, the memmap device kind psg8 (memmap.device.psg8, unknown-default-chosen); exercised by input.port.upper-byte, input.port.unplugged-is-idle, input.idle.p0, input.idle.p1, psg.port.upper-byte-zero, psg.port.idle-ff and memmap.width.psg8-low-byte-upper-zero. Hardware items: D10-INP-03, D10-INP-04.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-13 (D-16, D6). Phase 5 (D-04): both defaults are labelled; the upper-byte default is the memmap device kind psg8 fill.

discrepancies.topic: Read of a port the PSG drives as output
discrepancies.sources: SRC-bsr-2609 places the hand controllers on the sound chip's two 8-bit I/O ports. No source read by the project gives the value a CPU read returns from a port whose direction is set to output, with switches open or closed.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: input.port_output_read = latch: a read of a port whose R7 direction bit is 1 returns the stored latch value (low byte); a write always stores the latch; no contention is modelled when a switch grounds a driven pin. Core input stays logical switch state whatever the port direction.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: set each port to output, write known values and read them back with switches open and closed
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field input.port_output_read (unknown-default-chosen, latch); exercised by input.port.direction-output-reads-latch, input.port.write-latch-in-input-mode, input.port.per-port-direction, psg.port.output-reads-latch-0 and psg.port.output-reads-latch-1. Hardware item: D10-INP-05.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-13 (D-16, D6). Phase 5 (D-04): the field input.port_output_read carries this policy; the 8910 pages say each register is readable but not what an output-mode port read returns.

discrepancies.topic: Which connector is R14
discrepancies.sources: SRC-intv-wiki (Hand Controller, oldid 14808) gives reads at $01FE for the right controller and $01FF for the left. It is the only source (tier 4). Naming mismatch noted in Phase 5: SRC-consolemods-intv-pinouts labels port B the first player (1P) and port A the second (2P), while the wiki calls $01FE the right controller and $01FF the left; neither fixes the physical connector.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the core indexes controllers by PSG port only (0 = R14/$01FE, 1 = R15/$01FF), never by side or player; which physical connector feeds which port is a host or profile fact, recorded later as a profile field that names this entry.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: press one key on each physical controller and record which port reads it
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): no profile field names a connector; the core indexes ports only (field input.controllers counts the ports); exercised by input.port.independence, input.combo.ports-independent, input.port.per-port-direction and the single-control matrix on both ports. Hardware item: D10-INP-02.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-13 (D-16, D6). Phase 5 (D-04): ports stay named by index.

discrepancies.topic: Input application granularity
discrepancies.sources: No hardware source: a guest sees controller state only when an instruction reads a PSG port, and Phase 4 has no such read. The application rule is an architecture decision (D-14, A-04), not a hardware observation.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: an event takes effect at the first CPU-unit boundary whose start tick is at or after its at_tick; hardware may differ by up to one instruction, so this is a contract with a profile-flag reversal path, not a hardware claim.
discrepancies.resolver: test: input.boundary.start-minus-1, input.boundary.start and input.boundary.start-plus-1 pass (plan 05-05, the poll start tick observed by single-stepping); input.slice.guest-visible, run.input.* and run.fuzz.* keep the unit-start rule independent of slicing
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): the contract is exercised by input.boundary.start-minus-1, input.boundary.start, input.boundary.start-plus-1 (events at s-1 and s are seen by the poll starting at s, an event at s+1 only by the next poll), input.slice.guest-visible, input.iso.interleaved-instances and the runner scenario variants of diag-ctrl-psg-pass (one-tick-apart order, 1-tick and 7-tick slicing). It is a project contract, not a hardware statement: the entry stays open because a real console may differ by up to one instruction.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-13 (D-14, D-16, A-04). Refining the rule later changes goldens that carry input. Phase 5 (D-05): now guest-visible; the Phase 5 resolver is the named instruction-granularity test.

discrepancies.topic: Boot stub cartridge entry and stack
discrepancies.sources: project conventions of the Phase 4 boot stub ($5000 entry, $0340 stack); no hardware or first-party source
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the stub jumps to $5000 with R6=$0340; Phase 6/7 may change both with a new stub contract number
discrepancies.resolver: test: run.stub.path and run.diag.predicate (stub contract 1)
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 04-16 (D-28, D-31). fixtures/FX-boot-stub/boot-stub.listing.txt (contract 1) and fixtures/FX-diag-cpu-1/diag-cpu-1.listing.txt rely on both values; the predicate of data/golden/diag-cpu-1.expect asserts R6 = 0340 and [0206] = 0340 under this convention. Changing either value is a new stub contract number and new expected values, not an edit of the old ones.

discrepancies.topic: AY-3-8910 data sheet applied to the AY-3-8914-class part, and the chip step
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet pages are for the AY-3-8910/8912 (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 204-210, printed 5-23..5-29; SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 299-305); the console part is named AY-3-8914 by SRC-bsr-2609 and no 8914 page was found (C11). The divide chains on printed page 5-26 (input clock by 16, then by the period) fix the tone, noise and envelope step in PSG chip clocks only through the inference that a square wave toggles every half period.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: one PSG step is 8 PSG chip clocks (psg.clocks_per_step 8, tag inference): tone half-period P steps, noise shift every 2 NP steps, envelope step every 2 EP steps; the AY-3-8910 pages are applied to the 8914-class part by inference.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a tone of known period and compare the edge spacing with the profile
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile fields psg.clocks_per_step (inference, 8), psg.noise.steps_per_np, psg.envelope.steps_per_ep and psg.mixer.bits (inference) carry the chain; exercised by psg.profile.clocks-per-step, psg.profile.steps-per-np-ep, psg.profile.mixer-bits, psg.tone.rate-p1, rate-p2, rate-p3, rate-p255, rate-p256, rate-p4095, psg.noise.rate-np1.. and psg.env.rate-ep1..; the fault PSG_STEP_IS_16_CLOCKS fails them. Hardware item: D10-PSG-01.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-09, D-12). Profile fields psg.clocks_per_step and the PSG rules tagged 8910-primary-derived reference this entry.

discrepancies.topic: PSG register address permutation and the R8/R10 amplitude layouts
discrepancies.sources: The Intellivision order of the 16 registers at $01F0..$01FF is a permutation of the data sheet order and comes from community documentation only (SRC-intv-wiki PSG.oldid-14940, SRC-community-emu-docs; tier 4). The data sheet numbers registers in octal (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 207, printed 5-26: R10, R11, R12 amplitude, R13 and R14 envelope period, R15 shape, R16 and R17 ports). The 8914 amplitude register layout (4 bit fixed, 1 bit mode versus a wider field) is not documented.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: psg.regmap is the table in data/psg/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt (16 CPU addresses with role, GI octal number, write mask and read mask); stores keep value AND wmask; reads give reg AND rmask with bits 15..8 zero; no side effects.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: write distinct values to each of $01F0..$01FF with sound disabled and read each back
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.regmap (tier4-community) held to data/psg/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt by psg.regmap.matches-literal and the gate step psg-vectors; exercised by psg.reg.* (31 cases), psg.reg.map-amplitude, psg.reg.distinct-values, psg.reg.no-mirror and the judge self-controls psg.judge.regmap-literal-changed and psg.judge.mask-row-changed. Hardware item: D10-PSG-06.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-08, D-12). Profile field psg.regmap references this entry. The register-address literal is a tier 4 transcription.

discrepancies.topic: Noise generator polynomial, seed and output sense
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet defines a noise frequency (divide chain by 16 and the 5-bit period) but not a shift-register width, polynomial or seed (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 207, printed 5-26). Community documents give an LFSR mask that is not maximal.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: psg.noise.lfsr is a right-shifting Galois LFSR of width 17, mask $12000, seed $00001, output bit 0, no inversion (cycle length 131,071); the community mask $14000 is a one-field edit and has a non-maximal cycle length.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a noise-only channel and compare the bit pattern with the profile LFSR
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.noise.lfsr (unknown-default-chosen) is read by the engine, not hard-coded (fault PSG_NOISE_TAP_HARDCODED); exercised by psg.noise.lfsr-maximal-period, psg.noise.lfsr-alt-period, psg.noise.lfsr-first-bits, psg.profile.noise-taps and psg.noise.level-seq-np1. The first-bits convention (the output after each shift) was fixed by the blind second read (docs/psg/second-read-record-noise.md). Hardware item: D10-PSG-02.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-10, D-12). Profile field psg.noise.lfsr references this entry.

discrepancies.topic: Envelope step rate and restart on shape write
discrepancies.sources: The page gives the envelope divide chain (input clock by 256, then by the 16-bit period, then a further 16 for the 16-state cycle) and labels the period in Fig. 3 as the duration of one cycle (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 207 and 208, printed 5-26 and 5-27). Whether the counter restarts when R15 is written is not printed on these pages; community documents say it does.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: one envelope step is 16 EP chip clocks (2 EP PSG steps), a 16-state cycle is 256 EP chip clocks; a write to the shape register restarts the generator at the first state of the chosen shape.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture the envelope at two periods and the effect of rewriting R15 mid-cycle

discrepancies.topic: Port direction bit order of register R7
discrepancies.sources: Register R7 bits B7 and B6 choose the direction of the two I/O ports (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 207, printed 5-26); the figure labels the cell Input Enable and the page prints no sentence for the sense. The overbar of that cell was not resolvable on the 300 dpi render of plan 05-01.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: psg.mixer.port_dir_bits: B6 selects the direction of port 0 ($01FE) and B7 of port 1 ($01FF), 1 = output. The profile field carries the tag unknown-default-chosen because the page prints no sentence for the sense and a community page orders the two bits the other way; plan 05-12 aligned this text with the profile field (earlier text and decision D-04 said inference, which is the same unresolved status under the weakest-field rule).
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: set each R7 direction bit and observe whether the port still follows the pins
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.mixer.port_dir_bits (unknown-default-chosen, value A 6, B 7, output 1); exercised by psg.port.direction-bit-order, psg.profile.mixer-bits, input.port.direction-input-reads-pins, input.port.direction-output-reads-latch, input.port.r7-other-bits-ignored and the judge self-control input.judge.direction-sense-flipped. Hardware item: D10-PSG-11.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-04, D-12). Profile field psg.mixer.port_dir_bits references this entry.

discrepancies.topic: Register decode aliasing and mirrors
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet says the 16 registers occupy a 16-word block of a 1,024-word space selected by A9, A8 and the high address bits, which are mask programmable (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 205, printed 5-24). Whether the console decodes the block more than once is not documented.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: psg.mirrors = none: only $01F0..$01FF decode to the PSG; no alias.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: address-map probe of the words around $01F0..$01FF and the blocks 1024 words apart
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.mirrors (unknown-default-chosen, none); exercised by psg.reg.no-mirror and the memmap probe cases. Hardware item: D10-PSG-10.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-08, D-12). Profile field psg.mirrors references this entry.

discrepancies.topic: Read-back of the amplitude register R10 and of the shape register
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet says each of the 16 registers is readable (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 205, printed 5-24) and the register figure marks only low bits as used; the community register table reads the shape register as zero. The behaviour of the unused bits is not printed.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the read mask of the amplitude registers is $003F, of the shape register $0000 (reads zero, the tier 4 claim); the 8910 text would read it back, a one-field reversal.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: write all ones to the amplitude and shape registers and read them back
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): the read masks of profile field psg.regmap (tier4-community; amplitude 0x003F, shape 0x0000); exercised by psg.reg.shape-reads-zero, psg.reg.map-amplitude and psg.reg.amp-b, psg.reg.amp-c; the shape register read-back is excluded from the claims CL-0014 and CL-0015. Hardware item: D10-PSG-07.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-08, D-12). The psg.regmap read masks reference this entry.

discrepancies.topic: PSG chip clock ratio and phase
discrepancies.sources: The ratio of the PSG chip clock to the crystal is not printed for the console. The AY-3-8910 pages give the input clock range 1.0 to 2.0 MHz (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 209, printed 5-28); the community tone formula uses the crystal divided by 32 times the period (SRC-community-emu-docs); an emulator hint uses the crystal divided by 2 (tier 5, never evidence).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: ticks_per_psg_clock = 2 (PSG chip clock = crystal/2, tag inference), psg.clock_phase_ticks = 0 counted from reset.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: capture a tone of known period against the video timing, and measure the PSG clock pin
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile fields ticks_per_psg_clock (inference, 2) and psg.clock_phase_ticks (unknown-default-chosen, 0); exercised by psg.tone.rate-p1.., psg.sample.absolute-grid-from-reset, psg.sample.grid-stamp and psg.profile.clocks-per-step. Hardware item: D10-PSG-09.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-09, D-12). Profile fields ticks_per_psg_clock and psg.clock_phase_ticks reference this entry.

discrepancies.topic: PSG power-on and reset state beyond zero
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet says a low reset pin resets all registers to zero (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 205, printed 5-24) and says nothing about the counters, the noise register or the envelope. Whether the console ties the reset pin to the system reset is not documented.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: psg.reset: registers zero, tone outputs 0, tone counters empty (reload on the first step), noise register = seed, envelope held at its first state; the PSG is reset with the machine.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10 owner hardware: read the registers and capture the first samples after power-on and after a console reset
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.reset (unknown-default-chosen); exercised by psg.reset.power-on-zero, psg.reset.regs-zero, psg.reset.dirty-file-cleared, psg.reseng.reset-state, psg.reseng.silent-after-reset, psg.reseng.envelope-held-zero, psg.sample.silent-after-reset and psg.tone.first-edge-step1. Hardware item: D10-PSG-08.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-10, D-12). Profile field psg.reset references this entry.

discrepancies.topic: Write-effect instant, tie rule and sample alignment
discrepancies.sources: No source gives the instant within a CPU cycle at which a register write takes effect on the chip, nor the order of a write and a chip step at the same instant; the project contract is an architecture decision (D-16), like C67.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: a sample at tick k*16 observes writes stamped before k*16 (step first, then write); psg.write_strobe_ticks = 0; samples are stamped on an absolute grid from reset.
discrepancies.resolver: test: psg.sample.write-effect-boundary, psg.log.effect-boundary, psg.sample.grid-stamp, psg.sample.wrapper-stamp and psg.slice.tone-write-mid-slice pass (plans 05-06 and 05-08); a hardware reading is a D10 refinement
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile fields psg.write_strobe_ticks (unknown-default-chosen, 0) and psg.sample_period_ticks (inference, 16); the contract (a sample at tick k*16 sees writes stamped before k*16) is exercised by the tests named in the resolver and by psg.sample.absolute-grid-from-reset. A project contract, not a hardware claim.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-13, D-16). A project contract, not a hardware claim; refining it changes audio goldens.

discrepancies.topic: Raw 16-bit write value in the log versus the 8-bit register
discrepancies.sources: The CPU writes a 16-bit bus word to each PSG register while the chip data bus is 8 bits wide (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 204-205, printed 5-23 and 5-24); which bits the chip latches is not documented.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the write log stores the raw 16-bit bus value; the register keeps value AND wmask (low byte only); the high byte is never driven into the chip.
discrepancies.resolver: test: psg.log.value-raw-16bit and psg.log.addr-low-nibble pass (plan 05-08)
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): profile field psg.regmap (write masks, tier4-community); exercised by psg.log.value-raw-16bit, psg.log.addr-low-nibble, psg.reg.tone-high-mask and psg.reg.noise-mask.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-13, D-12). Profile field psg.regmap write masks reference this entry.

discrepancies.topic: Octal versus decimal register numbering across sources
discrepancies.sources: The data sheet numbers registers in octal (R0..R7, R10..R17; SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 207, printed 5-26), while community documents number them in decimal 0..15; R14 and R15 in one list are the same ports as R16 and R17 in the other (SRC-intv-wiki, SRC-consolemods-intv-pinouts).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: every table of the project carries both numberings and names the register by role; no table uses a bare register number.
discrepancies.resolver: test: the second blind read of data/psg/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt and the psg-vectors step (rule PSG-R02)
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 5 close-out (plan 05-12): the transcription hazard is guarded by profile field psg.regmap (both numberings in every row of data/psg/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt) and rule PSG-R02 through psg.regmap.matches-literal and the gate step psg-vectors. The blind second read of the register literal (read with regs) is recorded: 28 vectors, 27 agree and 1 is not comparable because the blinded copy omitted a read address (docs/psg/second-read-record-regs.md); no disagreement.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 05-01 (D-12). A transcription hazard, not a hardware question.

discrepancies.topic: STIC register read-back: which registers return data and which bits
discrepancies.sources: No manufacturer page prints a register address or a read behaviour (Plan 06-01 re-read pdf 191, 192, 193 and 199 of SRC-gi-1980-catalog and pdf 462, 463, 464 and 470 of SRC-gi-1982-catalog: structure and electrical data only). The community pages call $0000-$003F readable and state the collision registers are read by interrupt routines (SRC-intv-wiki, STIC-oldid-15008, Memory-Map-oldid-14847); the data on another board that returns $00FF is a single report.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: every register is write-only and reads the undriven fill $FFFF except the collision registers $18-$1F, which read $FC00 OR the stored 10 bits; reserved addresses read the fill.
discrepancies.resolver: pending: a tier 1 to 3 STIC register description, or the Phase 7 reader diagnostic on owner hardware (read-back of all 64 addresses)
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by the rmask and fill of each row of the register literal (data/stic/intv-2609-ntsc-family-p1.regmap.literal.txt) and memmap.device.stic14; default: write-only registers read $FFFF; exercised by stic.reg.write-only-reads-ffff, stic.reg.collision-readback, stic.reg.reserved-drops, stic.reg.masks, stic.table.matches-literal and the self-control stic.judge.register-row-changed. Final (plans 08-04, 08-05 and 08-08): the MOB register bit roles are the 48 rows of data/video/mob.literal.txt (conf C81, one lineage), checked by the shared row-grammar function of tools/check/video.cmake and exercised by video.mob.register-bit-roles (every non-ignored bit changes the plane or a collision register, every ignored bit changes nothing) with the self-control video.judge.mob-role-swapped; the collision registers still read $FC00 OR the stored ten bits (stic.reg.collision-readback, video.collision.read-no-effect) and the logged note that bits 15 and 14 read 0 is not acted on: every guest read of this project masks with 03FF (the program ivs-diag-stic-2 does, claim CL-0027).
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 06-01 (D-22, A-11). Extends C60. One rmask field per register changes the default. Source note ids: register note C81. Plan 08-03 (D-08) adds, logged only and not acted on: a later reverse-engineering note of the same author as the community register description (one lineage, observation of one other board) says bits 15 and 14 of STIC register reads are 0 and the other unimplemented bits read 1, with one exception in a reserved address; the guests of this project mask every collision read with 03FF. The MOB register bit roles are the rows of data/video/mob.literal.txt (conf C81, one lineage).

discrepancies.topic: Display-enable strobe at $0020: read effect, deadline, late strobe and per-frame re-strobe
discrepancies.sources: The community page names $0020 the active display strobe (SRC-intv-wiki, STIC-oldid-15008); no source states whether a read strobes, how long after the frame start a strobe is accepted, or whether one strobe lasts more than a frame.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: a write to $0020 inside the register window sets the display latch for the current frame and the latch is cleared at every frame start; a read of $0020 has no effect; the value written is ignored; a strobe outside the window is dropped.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10-VID-08 owner diagnostic with strobes at swept offsets and a frame capture

discrepancies.topic: Mechanism of the register and graphics-memory access windows
discrepancies.sources: The system RAM page (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 199, SRC-gi-1982-catalog pdf 470) prints a bus copy mode entered on the interrupt acknowledge and left at the first bus acknowledge edge, and the STIC page (pdf 191) says the CPU control bus is ignored outside CPU mode; the community windows are lengths in cycles (C1, C2). Neither page prints how the two relate.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: a pure frame-position schedule: the register window is the first 2,000 cycles of a frame and the graphics-memory window the first 3,780, whatever the display state (D-05); the bus copy mode event machine is the recorded alternative.
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10-VID-06 owner edge probes of the register and graphics-memory windows
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by the pure frame-position schedule of core/src/stic/stic_events.c with stic.reg_window_cpu_cycles and stic.gmem_window_cpu_cycles; the event machine is the recorded alternative; exercised by stic.events.edges, stic.window.applies-when-display-off, stic.profile.window-close, stic.profile.window-open and the self-control stic.judge.window-edge-moved.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 06-01 (D-22, A-11). Links C1, C2, C3. Reversal: a primary page that prints window events, or the D10 result. Source note ids: register note C83.

discrepancies.topic: Alias sensitivity of the STIC registers and the mode-select strobe
discrepancies.sources: The memory map page says a read of $4021, $8021 or $C021 during the first vertical blank period selects Color Stack mode although the CPU gets no STIC data, lists $0040-$007F as STIC-responsive read only, and the alias writes as register writes (SRC-intv-wiki, Memory-Map-oldid-14847).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: a read of $0021, $4021, $8021 or $C021 selects Color Stack mode through stic.mode_select_addrs; alias writes reach the register; reads of $0040-$007F have no effect; stic.alias_read_sensitive = 1.

The default value 1 is what the tests run; the value 0 of the field is only range-checked in the machine suite, not exercised end to end.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 06-01 (D-22, A-11). Extends C21 and C61. Source note ids: register note C84.

discrepancies.topic: Power-on state of the STIC: registers, mode and display latch
discrepancies.sources: No source states the state after power-on or reset. The Blue Sky Rangers page says the display is blacked out while the system program runs (SRC-bsr-2609).

discrepancies.topic: Stored widths and unknown bits of the STIC registers
discrepancies.sources: The community register diagrams show some bits as unknown (MOB X bits 11..13, the upper bits of Y and attribute) and the delay width is not stated (SRC-intv-wiki, STIC-oldid-15008). The 14 data pins of the STIC are printed (pdf 191).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the stored widths of the register literal: X 11 bits, Y 12, attribute 14, collision 10, color stack and border 4, delay 3, border extension 2; bits above are dropped and cannot be seen through the bus.
discrepancies.resolver: pending: a tier 1 to 3 STIC register description, or a read-back sweep on owner hardware
discrepancies.evidence: Phase 6 final (plan 06-14): carried by the stored widths of the register literal, enforced by the register file in core/src/stic/stic_regs.c; exercised by stic.reg.width, stic.reg.masks, stic.reg.reserved-drops.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 06-01 (D-22, A-11). Only the inspection report and the digest see the widths. Source note ids: register note C86.

discrepancies.topic: Collision register behaviour: clear on read, sticky set and the self bit
discrepancies.sources: No manufacturer or first-party page prints when collision bits are set or cleared (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 to 193, SRC-bsr-2609: the existence of three interaction classes only). The register description of the community lineage (SRC-community-emu-docs, read raw in plan 08-03) gives the bit roles, the sticky rule, the own-bit rule and the interaction-enable rule, and says nothing about a clear on read, a MOB at X 0, the border bit, off-screen positions or a display-off frame.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: collision bits are computed at the end of a displayed frame and ORed into the register file with or without a video buffer; a CPU write replaces the register under the write mask 03FF and a read has no side effect; the own bit is never SET by the frame writer, but a CPU write of the own bit is stored and read back although the source says the own bit reads 0 also when the CPU writes it (SRC-community-emu-docs@programming-stic-mob-controls): a pinned default that keeps the Phase 6 register literal and its tests unchanged; a MOB with X 0 does not interact, the border bit (bit 9) is a pixel inside the object grid outside the plane, off-screen collisions are detected and a display-off frame evaluates none (rules STIC-R44 and STIC-R45).
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10-VID-10
discrepancies.evidence: Plan 08-03 (oracle plan, no code): the collision truth table, section (d) of docs/video/diag-stic-2-derivation.md, and the pinned-default rows PD-3 to PD-7 of its section (i). Final (plans 08-05, 08-07 and 08-08): the derivable core is held by video.collision.truth-table (sixteen rows T1 to T16, a fresh scene each), video.collision.mob-mob-bits, mob-background-bit8, own-bit-never-set, intr-required, visibility-not-required, sticky-across-frames, or-at-frame-end, buffer-independent and slice-invariant, the judge video.judge.collision-truth-table-corrupt and the fault COLLISION_NOT_STICKY, and by the scenario diag-stic2-collision-pass (the sixteen words read in the routines of frames 3 and 4) with the program mutant STIC2-COLLIDE-APART. The pinned items: profile fields video.collision_x0_interacts (0), video.collision_border_bit (1), video.collision_offscreen (1) and video.collision_display_off (0), each tag unknown-default-chosen with a default-pinned test that flips it (video.collision.default-pinned.x0, .border-bit, .offscreen and .display-off); and, held by absence, a read with no side effect (video.collision.read-no-effect; flip: the existing field stic.mode_select_addrs and one access-effect row changed in a stack copy make the same read switch the mode) and a CPU write that replaces the register (video.collision.cpu-write-replaces). The own bit on a CPU write is pinned the same way (decision of plan 08-08): the source statement is SRC-community-emu-docs@programming-stic-mob-controls, the default keeps the write mask 03FF so a written own bit is stored, no scenario or frame depends on it (the program writes only 0 and cpu-write-replaces writes only values whose own bit is clear), and the Phase 6 register literal and tests are unchanged; owner hand-off D10-VID-10 (not performed; its procedure item records the value read after a write of the own bit). Claim exclusion: CL-0026 carries no read or clear semantics beyond sticky bits, no own bit on a CPU write, and no X coordinate 0, edge, off-screen or display-off result.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 06-01 (D-22, A-11). Source note ids: register note C87. Updated by plan 08-03 (D-06, D-09): the resolver is now the owner hand-off D10-VID-10 and the rules STIC-R44 and STIC-R45 pin the default. Plan 08-08 words the own bit on a CPU write as an explicit pinned default (the source says it reads 0, the profile keeps the write mask 03FF); the frozen oracle files are unchanged and the amendment is appended to section (k) of the derivation.

discrepancies.topic: Bus-window table: count, first start, pitch, hold and which rows

discrepancies.topic: Printed branch range against the decle arithmetic (the limit of the project assembler)
discrepancies.sources: The branch table prints the range of the unconditional branch as +1025 to -1024 (SRC-gi-cp1600-um-1975 pdf 54). With the 10-bit displacement decle (at most 03FF) and the stated formulas a forward branch reaches the address of the branch plus 2 plus 1023, which is plus 1025, and a backward branch reaches the address plus 1 minus 1023, which is minus 1022; the printed minus 1024 is not reproduced and the base of the printed numbers is not stated.
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the project assembler ivs_asm follows the decle limit in both directions (a displacement above 03FF is refused with asm-branch-range) and uses neither the printed range nor any wider displacement; the core derives a branch target from the printed formula only (C50) and has no range rule.
discrepancies.resolver: test: asm.boundary.branch-03ff (03FF accepted) and asm.neg.asm-branch-range (0400 refused) pin the assembler limit only; a statement of the base of the printed range in the manual, or the D10 branch probe named under C50, would say whether the printed minus 1024 is a different range or a different base
discrepancies.evidence: Plan 07-04 (D-17): tools/asm/asm.c computes the displacement as target minus (pc + 2) forward and (pc + 1) minus target backward, each at most 03FF, the formula the listing checker uses for the printed target; docs/diagnostics.md.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 07-04 (07-DISCUSS-assembler.md S3-6 and open item 7). Neighbour of C50. No hardware claim: it records only that the printed text and the decle arithmetic differ.

discrepancies.sources: The register description of the community lineage says a MOB with the priority bit set appears behind the background cards and that the ordering applies to the visible pixels of the MOB only (SRC-community-emu-docs, read raw in plan 08-03). It does not say whether a card pixel that is off (background color) hides the MOB. No manufacturer or first-party page prints a priority rule (SRC-gi-1980-catalog pdf 191 to 193, SRC-bsr-2609).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: a MOB with the priority bit set is hidden only where the background card pixel is on (card foreground, colored-squares colors 0 to 6); where the card pixel is off the MOB pixel shows (profile field video.mob_prio_hides = on-pixels; the flip all-pixels hides it behind every card pixel).

discrepancies.evidence: Plan 08-03 (oracle plan, no code): the rule and the pinned-default row PD-1 of docs/video/diag-stic-2-derivation.md section (i) were written before any renderer. Final (plans 08-04 and 08-08): carried by profile field video.mob_prio_hides (0 = on-pixels, tag unknown-default-chosen; the flip 1 = all-pixels), read by cmake/IvsSticTable.cmake into ivs_stic_params and applied in core/src/stic/stic_mob.c; pinned by the default-pinned test video.mob.default-pinned.prio-set, which asserts the default (39 MOB and 25 card positions) and then flips the one field in a stack copy of the parameters and requires the MOB positions to change; the derivable neighbour (a MOB with the priority bit clear in front of the cards, the lower index of two MOBs in front) is held by video.mob.prio-clear-front, video.mob.front-lower-index and video.mob.frame-priority-colour and guarded by the fault MOB_PRIORITY_SWAP. No frame, assert or marker depends on this case: no frame literal and no scenario sets the priority bit. Owner hand-off D10-VID-11 (not performed); claim exclusion: CL-0025 carries no priority-set pixel rule.
discrepancies.note: Raised by plan 08-03 (D-02, D-09, rule STIC-R43). One lineage; tier 4 only.

discrepancies.topic: Half-height MOB pixels, the line-resolved model and the published 159 x 96 plane
discrepancies.sources: The community lineage says a MOB is displayed with half pixels vertically when both Y size bits are clear, that is one TV line per pattern row, and the printed row is 2 lines (SRC-community-emu-docs, SRC-intv-wiki STIC-oldid-15008; C105 row-lines). The published plane has one row per 2 lines (D8), so a half-height pattern row has no plane row of its own.

It does not say whether the top strip is 8 plane rows or 8 lines, nor whether a strip moves with the delay.

discrepancies.topic: Delay: content of the exposed area, MOBs in it and the delay range
discrepancies.sources: The register description says the delay registers make the blank areas of the object field visible and that the blank area is filled with the background color as the display mode defines it (SRC-community-emu-docs, read raw in plan 08-03), which does not name one color index in either mode. A reverse-engineering note of the same author lists whether MOBs are visible in the rows exposed by vertical delay as still to be measured. The delay range is the stored width of the register literal (3 bits, C86).
discrepancies.default_policy: unknown-default-chosen: the exposed columns and rows are published as not displayed (profile field video.delay_exposed_fill = not-displayed; the flip border publishes the border color), a MOB is not drawn there (video.delay_mob_in_exposed = not-drawn; the flip drawn), the delay is 0 to 7 and a vertical delay does not change the bus-window schedule (C92).
discrepancies.resolver: measurement: D10-VID-12
discrepancies.evidence: Plan 08-03 (oracle plan, no code): rules STIC-R46 and STIC-R47, the pinned-default rows PD-10 to PD-13 of docs/video/diag-stic-2-derivation.md section (i) and frame F-M7 (the exposed rectangles unknown, no hash).
